implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines turns the splitter into a flow operator: a Flow<Composite> becomes a Flow<Part> with transform, or with its shortcut flatMapConcat (which is @ExperimentalCoroutinesApi and is defined as map(transform).flattenConcat()), and the collector publishes each part with back-pressure supplied by the suspending chain. The API documentation explicitly warns that flatMapConcat is heavier than it looks and that a suspending operation inside a plain map is usually sufficient for application-specific flows, so use it only when one upstream element genuinely becomes many emissions. Reach for the collection form when the split is synchronous.
pitfalls: flatMapConcat concatenates strictly in order; flatMapMerge interleaves parts and destroys the order the composite implied.
A blocking call (JDBC, blocking HTTP) inside transform stalls the dispatcher thread - move it to withContext(Dispatchers.IO).
Flows are cold: a flow splitter that decodes the composite lazily re-decodes it for every collector unless it is shared.

variants.name: Lazy sequence splitting (Sequence.flatMap / sequence builder)
variants.implementation_notes: Without coroutines the splitter is an ordinary collection operation: flatMap applies a collection-valued function to each element and concatenates the results, and because sequences produce their elements while iterating, asSequence() keeps the split lazy so no intermediate collection is built. The sequence() builder goes one step further and emits parts one by one or in chunks of arbitrary size with yield/yieldAll, which is the direct analogue of a generator splitter. This form has no back-pressure of its own, so pacing must come from a paged send loop or from a coroutine boundary.
pitfalls: flatMap on a List receiver is eager and builds every part up front; only the Sequence receiver is lazy, so check which overload is in play for large composites.
Sequences are usually restartable but individual implementations may be single-use - the documentation calls this out, and a stored sequence that was iterated once may yield nothing.
Mixing eager chunked() (returns List<List<T>>) with lazy processing materialises the whole split.
